name: CBR-KBQA (Case-based Reasoning for Natural Language Queries over Knowledge Bases)
venue: EMNLP 2021 (Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, pages 9594-9611; ACL Anthology 2021.emnlp-main.755)
authors_affiliation: Rajarshi Das, Manzil Zaheer, Dung Thai, Ameya Godbole, Ethan Perez, Jay-Yoon Lee, Lizhen Tan, Lazaros Polymenakos, Andrew McCallum. Lead/primary affiliation: University of Massachusetts, Amherst (Das, Thai, Godbole, Lee, McCallum); other affiliations: New York University (Perez), Google Research (Zaheer), Amazon (Tan), EY Greece (Polymenakos).
code_url: [uncertain] (No dedicated official public repo for the EMNLP 2021 CBR-KBQA was located; the authors' related public repos are rajarshd/CBR-AKBC for the AKBC 2020 KB-completion work and rajarshd/CBR-SUBG for the ICML 2022 CBR-SUBG follow-up, not this paper)
task_domain: QA -- knowledge base question answering (KBQA) / semantic parsing: mapping complex natural language questions to executable SPARQL logical forms over Freebase.
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent, supervised semantic parsing for KBQA. Given a natural language query q and a symbolic KB K (full Freebase, ~45M entities / ~3B facts), generate an executable SPARQL logical form whose execution returns the answer set A. Supervision is gold (question, logical-form) pairs in a training set D. Setting is non-interactive at inference (one-shot retrieve-reuse-revise per query), but supports test-time addition of new human-labeled cases to the case memory without retraining. Weakly-supervised (question-answer only) baselines are also compared.
what_is_retrieved: cases -- specifically (question, logical-form/SPARQL-program) pairs (k-nearest-neighbor similar training queries and their gold logical forms) stored in a nonparametric case memory.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID leaning growing-memory: the primary store is a case memory seeded from the training set (offline), but it is explicitly designed to grow at inference by injecting new human-labeled or SimpleQuestions-derived cases without retraining (write-able episodic case memory). The revise step additionally grounds to the static external KB (Freebase relation neighborhood / TransE KB embeddings).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k retrieval objective: retrieve top-k=20 similar cases, optimized so that the union of their logical-form relations covers (recall@k) the relations needed by the target query. The retriever is evaluated by percentage of gold LF relations present in the top-k retrieved cases (recall@k), i.e. a coverage/completeness flavor of relation recall rather than a single-best ranking; downstream the reuse module composes from multiple retrieved cases.
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain] -- all four canonical CBR phases are implemented: Retrieve (RoBERTa KNN case retrieval), Reuse (BigBird seq2seq reuses LF components to generate an intermediate LF), Revise (align generated relations to KB neighborhood via TransE/RoBERTa to make LF executable), Retain (human-in-the-loop / SimpleQuestions cases are added to the KNN case memory at test time without retraining).
explicit_cbr_grounding: True. The work explicitly frames itself as case-based reasoning, cites Aamodt & Plaza (1994) for the Retrieve/Reuse/Revise CBR cycle and Schank (1982)/Kolodner for CBR origins, and defines a 'case' as an abstract problem-solution representation (question paired with executable logical form).
retrieval_unit: case (problem-solution): a (natural-language-question, executable-SPARQL-logical-form) pair. The query key is the question; the retrieved payload includes the full SPARQL program.
index_source: Hybrid construction: the retrievable case store is offline-induced from the training set D of (question, LF) pairs (precomputed and cached query representations), and is online/test-time-extendable by appending new cases (human-labeled simple cases or SimpleQuestions edges) to the KNN index without retraining.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (KNN index over normalized RoBERTa [CLS] question embeddings; inner-product / cosine similarity). The downstream revise step additionally consults the KB graph neighborhood, but the case index itself is a flat vector store.
retriever_type: Dense (learned bi-encoder): a RoBERTa-base encoder produces independent [CLS] embeddings per question; retrieval is inner-product / cosine top-k (DPR-style dense passage-retrieval design).
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive / weighted similarity supervision derived from downstream logical forms: fine-tuned with a weighted negative-log-likelihood (in-batch) loss where the weight w_ij between a query pair is the F1 overlap between the sets of KB relations in their gold logical forms (distant supervision from LFs). Entity spans are masked with probability p_mask (0.2 for CWQ, 0.5 otherwise) to emphasize relational rather than entity similarity. Initialized from pre-trained RoBERTa-base; trained ~10 epochs, selected by recall@20 on validation.
query_construction: Raw natural language question is encoded directly; named entities are detected by an NER tagger and masked with a [BLANK] symbol (probability p_mask) during retrieval to emphasize relational similarity. For the reuse step, the query string is augmented by appending each entity's KB id after its surface mention (e.g. 'What do Jamaican m.03_r3 people speak?').
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval per input question; the whole question is the query, retrieved once before generation. No per-step or trajectory-level re-retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: One-shot: retrieve top-k cases once per query before generation. (The only iterative aspect is the offline/human-in-the-loop addition of cases to the index, not per-inference iterative retrieval.)
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per incoming query at the start of the pipeline (no confidence/uncertainty/learned-router trigger).
reranking: None. No explicit reranking stage; the top-k=20 cases by dense similarity are passed directly to the reuse module.
retrieved_context_refinement: None at the retrieval stage (top-k cases are concatenated directly into the BigBird encoder). A post-generation refinement exists in the separate Revise step (relation alignment to KB), but no decompose/distill/compress/filter operation is applied to the retrieved cases themselves.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tools/APIs; retrieved units are question-LF cases, not tool documents).
index_content_separation: N/A -- cases (question + full SPARQL program) are stored and loaded together; no lightweight-index-then-heavy-content progressive-disclosure separation. Query vectors are precomputed/cached but the case content is loaded directly.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no tool index / external API protocol). The case index is static-after-training but manually extendable by appending cases; no CRUD auto-sync, RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling protocol.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling; no tools).
how_retrieved_used: Case adaptation / prompt(context) augmentation for generation: the retrieved (question, LF) cases are concatenated with the input query and fed to a BigBird seq2seq generator (Reuse) which composes/reuses components of the retrieved logical forms to produce an intermediate LF; the LF is then revised by aligning generated relations to the KB. Retrieved cases also serve as a parametric training signal (model learns to reuse) and at test time enable copying unseen relations from injected cases.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan/generate (one-shot exemplars at generation time): retrieval happens once up front; the k cases condition a single seq2seq generation of the full logical form (the 'plan'), followed by a post-hoc revise/alignment step. Not interleaved per-step, not inside tree search.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer / per-query: a single retrieval and a single conditioned generation produce one logical form per query; retrieval is not woven per CoT-step or per token.
adaptation_mechanism: LLM/seq2seq-prompted adaptation plus execution-grounded revision: (1) Reuse -- a BigBird seq2seq model conditioned on the retrieved cases generates a new (intermediate) logical form, reusing/recombining components of the retrieved LFs (a learned, non-verbatim adaptation, regularized by a KLD term toward the no-case prediction); (2) Revise -- a non-learned alignment that replaces generated relations with the most semantically similar relation edge that actually exists in the query entity's local KB neighborhood (via pre-trained TransE KB embeddings, or RoBERTa surface-form similarity) to make the LF executable.
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected is the raw case text: the retrieved question string plus its executable SPARQL program, concatenated with [SEP] separators on the encoder side (q [SEP] q1' [SEP] l1' ... qk' [SEP] lk'). No distillation/compression; it is the literal (question, logical-form) pair.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single demonstration / case at the level of a problem-solution pair (question + executable logical form). Not a distilled strategy or abstracted workflow -- the literal prior solved cases are retrieved and their LF components reused.
noise_robustness_mechanism: (1) Reuse-step KL-divergence regularization term forcing the with-cases prediction not to deviate too far from the no-case prediction (guards against over-reliance on possibly-irrelevant retrieved cases); (2) entity masking during retrieval so similarity reflects relational structure rather than entity overlap; (3) the Revise step corrects relations that do not execute (domain mismatch / KB incompleteness) by aligning to existing KB edges. No explicit relevance-evaluator/self-reflection on retrieved cases.
memory_type: episodic case memory (nonparametric KNN case store of (question, logical-form) pairs); the knowledge for revision is also a graph (KB) but the retrievable memory is episodic/case-based.
write_back: True (limited / manual): new cases (human-labeled simple cases, or SimpleQuestions-derived single-relation cases) can be written into the KNN case memory at inference time to fix erroneous predictions or cover unseen relations, without any retraining. There is no automatic self-generated experience write-back during normal inference.
online_growth: Yes -- the case memory can grow at test/deployment time: an expert or curated source adds new cases to the KNN index (0 gradient steps, ~2 seconds), which the retriever can then surface. This is the paper's central controllability/point-fix contribution. Growth is human/curation-driven, not autonomous.
write_back_trigger: Human-validated / on-demand: writes are triggered by a human-in-the-loop point-fix (an expert injects a simple case to correct a wrong prediction) or by curated import from SimpleQuestions; not automatic, not on every success/failure, not reflective.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only / positive cases: the memory stores correct (question, gold-LF) cases. Failed/negative trajectories are not stored as retrievable items; the point-fix mechanism responds to a detected failure by adding a new correct case, not by storing the failure itself. (Negatives appear only transiently as in-batch negatives during contrastive retriever training.)
memory_evolution_update: Append-only: new cases are added to the KNN index; existing stored cases are not mutated, merged, deltas-updated, or pruned.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No -- retrieval is a fixed similarity top-k (dense cosine KNN). The retriever encoder is learned (contrastive on LF-relation-overlap weights), but case selection at inference is a fixed top-k nearest-neighbor rule, not an RL/learned selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No -- single-model private case memory; no multi-agent or cross-framework experience sharing.
benchmarks: WebQSP (WebQuestionsSP), ComplexWebQuestions (CWQ), Compositional Freebase Questions (CFQ; MCD1/MCD2/MCD3 splits). Underlying KB: full Freebase (~45M entities, ~3B facts). Also a held-out unseen-relation generalization split of WebQSP and a human-in-the-loop (HITL) OOV-relation experiment; SimpleQuestions used as a source of simple cases. Entity linking via ELQ + FACC1.
benchmark_family: QA / multi-hop KBQA (semantic parsing to SPARQL over a knowledge base); CFQ specifically targets compositional generalization.
baselines: Supervised: T5-11B (Raffel et al. 2020), T5-11B+Revise (their revise step applied to T5), STAGG (Yih et al. 2016). Weakly-supervised: GraftNet, PullNet, EmbedKGQA (WebQSP); KBQA-GST, QGG, PullNet, DynAS/Alibaba (CWQ). On CFQ, T5-11B (Furrer et al. 2020). Generalization/point-fix experiments compare against a baseline (BigBird/BART-style) transformer that must be fine-tuned.
key_metrics: Strict exact-match accuracy (Acc; predicted answer list from executing generated SPARQL must exactly match gold answer list), plus Precision/Recall/F1 of answer entities. Retriever evaluated intrinsically by recall@k (fraction of gold LF relations covered by top-k cases). CFQ reported as accuracy per MCD split.
headline_result: On the hidden CWQ test set, CBR-KBQA reaches 67.1% accuracy (P 70.4 / R 71.9 / F1 70.0), outperforming the prior state-of-the-art (the abstract states 'by 11% on accuracy'; vs the best reported prior weakly-supervised system DynAS 50.0 and T5-11B 52.4). On WebQSP it reaches 69.9% accuracy (F1 72.8), >6 points over the best baseline; on CFQ MCD-mean 78.1 vs T5-11B 67.7.
ablations: (1) Cases ablation (Table 9): baseline K=0 (no cases) vs CBR-KBQA K=20 -- 67.2->69.9 on WebQSP and 65.8->67.1 on CWQ, showing retrieved cases help; removing the KL-divergence regularization term drops to 68.1 (WebQSP) / 66.7 (CWQ). (2) Revise-step ablation (Table 5): +Revise(TransE) improves accuracy 69.43->70.00 (WebQSP, +0.57) and 65.95->67.11 (CWQ, +1.16); TransE alignment beats RoBERTa surface-form alignment; revise also improves the T5 baseline (>3 F1 points on CWQ). (3) Unseen-relation generalization (Table 6): adding cases to the index (0 gradient steps) lifts held-out accuracy from 0 to 70.6% with no forgetting on the initial set (69.4), whereas a fine-tuned transformer suffers catastrophic forgetting. (4) HITL OOV experiment (Table 7): adding cases raises OOV-question performance from 0 to ~36 F1 / 32.89 Acc without retraining. (5) Novel-combination analysis: CBR-KBQA answers more compositional-reasoning questions correctly than T5 (CWQ 270 vs 205; CFQ 3886 vs 3351).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- intrinsic retriever quality is reported separately (recall@k of gold LF relations in top-k cases; retriever selected by recall@20) and entity-linking P/R/F1 (Table 2) is reported separately, in addition to end-to-end answer accuracy/F1.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (answer exact-match accuracy / F1 from executing the generated SPARQL). Some intermediate/process signals are reported: retriever recall@k, entity-linking P/R/F1, and analysis of how many compositional-reasoning questions are answered correctly; but no per-step reasoning-faithfulness scoring.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Argues a strong parameter-efficiency tradeoff: CBR-KBQA uses orders-of-magnitude fewer parameters than T5-11B (generator is BigBird with 6+6 sparse-attention layers initialized from BART-base) yet outperforms it on all benchmarks, with lower carbon footprint. Controllability efficiency: a point-fix (adding a case to the index) takes 0 gradient steps / ~2 seconds vs fine-tuning a transformer (100-300 gradient steps) which causes catastrophic forgetting. Query representations are precomputed/cached. No explicit per-query latency/API-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k: k=20 retrieved cases concatenated into the BigBird encoder; BigBird's sparse attention is the enabling lever for the long concatenated context (BART/T5 512-token full-attention encoders cannot fit as many cases). Decoding uses beam size 5. k is fixed (not adaptive/precision-driven).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper). For reference, datasets used: WebQSP ~4737 questions, 56 domains, 661 unique relations, up to 2-hop; CWQ extends WebQSP to up to 4-hop multi-hop (composition 45% / conjunction 45% / comparative 5% / superlative 5%); CFQ targets compositional generalization (MCD1/2/3). KB is full Freebase (~45M entities, ~3B facts).
builds_on: Dense passage retrieval / DPR (Karpukhin et al. 2020; Das et al. 2019); BigBird sparse-attention transformer (Zaheer et al. 2020); BART (Lewis et al. 2020); RoBERTa; TransE KB embeddings (Bordes et al. 2013) for revise alignment; entity-independent relational representations via entity masking (Soares et al. 2019); ELQ entity linker (Li et al. 2020) + FACC1; classical CBR (Schank 1982; Aamodt & Plaza 1994; Kolodner); the authors' earlier CBR for KB completion (Das et al. 2020 'A Simple Approach to Case-Based Reasoning in Knowledge Bases', AKBC).
contrasts_with: Retrieve-and-edit (Hashimoto et al. 2018) -- conditions on a single retrieved example and lacks an explicit revise step, unlike CBR-KBQA which reuses partial logic from multiple cases and revises against the KB. REALM (Guu et al. 2020) and RAG (Lewis et al. 2020) -- retrieve relevant text passages from a nonparametric memory, whereas CBR-KBQA retrieves similar queries and reuses relational structure of their logical forms. Massive parametric seq2seq models (T5-11B) that memorize patterns in parameters and cannot add new relations without retraining (catastrophic forgetting). KB-traversal/weakly-supervised models (GraftNet, PullNet, EmbedKGQA, STAGG).
lineage: Group A (in-context-learning / demonstration retrieval). Foundational neuro-symbolic CBR-with-retrieval: a nonparametric (question, logical-form) case memory plus a retrieve-and-reuse(-revise) pipeline usable with new cases without retraining -- a lineage origin for case/demonstration retrieval and CBR-style retrieve-reuse-revise in later LLM agent / KBQA work (e.g. its own follow-up CBR-SUBG, ICML 2022).
